title: Rounding decimals
summary: Zoom in between a number's two neighbours and see which is nearer: to the nearest whole number, to 1 and 2 decimal places, and to significant figures. Then find every number that rounds to the same value.
guide: To round a number, find its two neighbours and see which one it is nearer to. For example, 3.7 is between 3 and 4 and is nearer 4, so 3.7 rounds to 4 (to the nearest whole number).
If a number is exactly halfway, like 3.5, we round up.
Rounding is not the same as cutting off (truncating). Cutting off just drops the digits: 3.7 becomes 3. Rounding picks the nearest: 3.7 becomes 4.
"To 1 decimal place" (1 d.p.) means to the nearest tenth; "to 2 decimal places" means to the nearest hundredth.
The small line at the top shows the whole number line; the coloured piece is the part shown magnified underneath.

engine.label-line: Number line: tap to place a point

nearest-whole.title: To the nearest whole number
nearest-whole.prompt: The point on the line is 3.7. Round it to the nearest whole number. Predict first: is it nearer 3 or 4?
nearest-whole.hint: The taller mark in the middle is 3.5. 3.7 is past it.
nearest-whole.success: Well done! 3.7 is nearer 4, so it rounds to 4.
nearest-whole.why: Cutting off 3.7 gives 3; rounding gives 4. Which is closer to the real value, and why?
nearest-whole.model: 4. From 3.7 to 4 is only 0.3, but from 3.7 to 3 is 0.7. Rounding always gives the nearest number.

feedback.cut-off: That's cutting off the decimal, not rounding. Is 3.7 nearer 3 or 4?
feedback.no-mark: You've lost the decimal point. 3.7 is between 3 and 4, not 37.
feedback.too-big: The answer should be one of the two neighbours: 3 or 4.
feedback.too-small: The answer should be one of the two neighbours: 3 or 4.

nearest-tenth.title: To 1 decimal place
nearest-tenth.prompt: Here the part from 2.4 to 2.5 is magnified. Round 2.46 to 1 decimal place: put a point on the tenth it is nearer to.
nearest-tenth.hint: Halfway between 2.4 and 2.5 is 2.45. 2.46 is past halfway.
nearest-tenth.why: To round to 1 decimal place, why do you only need to look at the hundredths digit (6)?
nearest-tenth.model: The hundredths digit tells you whether the number has passed halfway between the two tenths (2.45). If it is 5 or more, the number is nearer the next tenth up.

feedback.count: Put one point on the nearer tenth.
feedback.too-small: Put the point on one of the two tenths, 2.4 or 2.5. 2.4 is what you get by cutting off, but 2.46 is past halfway (2.45).
feedback.too-big: Put the point on one of the two tenths, 2.4 or 2.5.

bounds.title: What rounds to 3.5?
bounds.prompt: Lots of numbers round to 3.5 (to 1 d.p.). Mark the smallest of them with a point. Put the second point on the first number that no longer rounds to 3.5, but to 3.6.
bounds.hint: A number exactly halfway between two tenths rounds up. Where is halfway between 3.4 and 3.5? And between 3.5 and 3.6?
bounds.success: Well done! Every number from 3.45 up to (but not including) 3.55 rounds to 3.5. 3.45 is the lower bound and 3.55 the upper bound: 3.45 ≤ x < 3.55
bounds.model: 3.55 is exactly halfway between 3.5 and 3.6, and halfway rounds up, so 3.55 rounds to 3.6. But anything just below it, like 3.549, still rounds to 3.5.

feedback.count: Put two points: one on the smallest number, one on the first number that rounds to 3.6.
feedback.wrong: Both points should be exactly halfway between two tenths: one between 3.4 and 3.5, one between 3.5 and 3.6.

nearest-hundredth.title: To 2 decimal places
nearest-hundredth.prompt: Round 0.367 to 2 decimal places and type the answer. The line magnifies the part from 0.36 to 0.37.
nearest-hundredth.hint: The thousandths digit is 7, which is 5 or more, so the number has passed halfway between the two hundredths.
nearest-hundredth.why: 0.37 has fewer digits than 0.367. So why is it bigger?
nearest-hundredth.model: 0.37 is the same as 0.370, and 370 thousandths is more than 367 thousandths. The number of digits doesn't tell you the size of a decimal.

feedback.too-small: 0.36 is what you get by cutting off. Is 0.367 nearer 0.36 or 0.37?
feedback.too-big: Round to 2 decimal places: two digits after the point. 0.4 is rounded to 1 decimal place.

sig-figs.title: To 2 significant figures
sig-figs.prompt: Round 0.0468 to 2 significant figures. The line magnifies the part from 0.046 to 0.047.
sig-figs.hint: The first significant figure is the first digit that isn't zero: the 4. The second is the 6. Look at the next digit, 8.
sig-figs.why: Why aren't the zeros at the start of 0.0468 significant figures?
sig-figs.model: They only show where the decimal point is (the place value), not how precise the number is. 0.0468 is 468 ten-thousandths: the significant figures start at the 4.

feedback.too-small: 0.046 is cutting off. The next digit is 8 (5 or more), so round up.
feedback.too-big: The zeros at the front don't count. Keep two figures starting from the 4: 0.04… then round. 0.05 has only 1 significant figure.
